title: No trump can save this trick

feedback.title: A guaranteed trick in Sans
feedback.summary: East has already shown void in Hearts, and in Sans only Hearts can win this trick — North and West have already played below the king, and East cannot add a Heart to challenge it.
points: The earlier trick shows East playing a club when Hearts were led, so East holds no more Hearts this hand.
In Sans, a card that cannot follow the led suit can never win the trick — East's response cannot beat any Heart you play.
No higher Heart remains to be added to this trick: North and West have already played, and East cannot follow suit.

feedback.title: Giving away a trick you can already win
feedback.summary: Playing the two lets the nine of Hearts win instead; the king guarantees this trick in Sans, and the target's exact estimate still requires both of the two remaining tricks.
points: The earlier trick already showed East void in Hearts, so nothing remaining in this trick can beat the king.
In Sans, East's forced off-suit card cannot win this trick regardless of what East plays.
The target's exact estimate still requires both remaining tricks; giving up a trick the king guarantees moves it into the harder, uncertain remainder.

author_notes: Second void-tracking scenario (EC-042). Sans removes the usual trump risk entirely: once East is confirmed void in the led suit, no card East holds can win this trick, making the king a fully certain winner rather than merely a probable one. Seat order corrected to the owner-confirmed North -> West -> South -> East rotation; East (not West) is the seat that plays after South.
